study_information.title: Decreased Bone Formation Explains Osteoporosis in a Genetic Mouse Model of Hemochromatosiss
study_information.summary: Osteoporosis may complicate iron-overload diseases such as genetic hemochromatosis, but the mechanisms are poorly understood. The authors analysed the impact of excess iron in Hfe-/- male mice, a model of human hemochromatosis, on osteoblast activity and bone microarchitecture using histomorphometry. Hfe-/- mice were sacrificed at 6 months and compared with wild-type controls. Iron-overloaded mice showed excess bone iron, a decreased bone formation rate, and microarchitectural impairment (lower trabecular bone volume and number, increased trabecular separation, and reduced connectivity and complexity). The findings support a negative effect of iron on osteoblast recruitment and/or function contributing to iron-related osteoporosis.
